analysis: The change set has four parts. (1) install.sh adds PROVIDER_CONFIG, PRODUCTION_COORD_URL, provider_websocket_url and bind_provider_coordinator, plus a `--bind-coordinator-test` entry point. The installer calls bind_provider_coordinator after the signed bundle is committed and before the Secure Enclave step, and exits 1 if it fails. Non-production coordinator URLs are written into provider.toml as wss://host/ws/provider. Plain ws:// is accepted only for localhost/127.0.0.1. Production removes any url. The host regex blocks TOML injection, and the awk edit preserves the other lines. This binding of provider to coordinator is the new attack surface, and it interacts with T-040 (Host-header-derived URLs when baseURL is unset), TB-002, A-008 and A-010. Signature and hash verification of the app bundle is unchanged, and the staged-app, fan-helper and App Attest logic is untouched. (2) install_sh_test.go adds a test that runs the served installer's bind function in four cases, plus the os/exec import. It only exercises dev and production base URLs, with no negative or hostile-host cases such as http to a remote host, a malformed host, or an existing url in other sections. (3) coordinator/cmd/devnet-seed/main.go is a new file whose content was not supplied (metadata only). I could not review it; it is a coverage gap and could handle seed credentials or ledger data (A-009, A-007). (4) coordinator/api/install.sh and the canonical scripts/install.sh must stay byte-identical (TestEmbeddedInstallerMatchesCanonicalSource); the canonical copy was not shown. Follow-up reviewers should check devnet-seed for production-reachability and secrets, and whether the provider's ProviderConfig.swift trusts the written url without further checks.

findings.detail: The new bind_provider_coordinator writes `[coordinator] url = wss://<host>/ws/provider` into ~/.config/darkbloom/provider.toml whenever COORD_URL is not exactly https://api.darkbloom.dev. COORD_URL comes from the coordinator's serve-time substitution, which falls back to the request Host/X-Forwarded-Proto when baseURL is unset (T-040). Previously a spoofed or poisoned installer URL only affected that one install run, because the bundle signature is pinned to the Developer ID requirement. Now a poisoned installer (cached, or served by a mis-configured coordinator) permanently points the provider at an attacker-controlled https host. That host would then receive the provider's registration, attestation blobs, challenge traffic and any login/provider-token flow on later `darkbloom start`/`login`/update runs. provider_websocket_url only checks the host regex and the http-localhost rule; it does not check an allowlist of Darkbloom domains. A user who ran the installer with a custom COORD_URL also has their existing `[coordinator] url` silently removed when installing from production, without confirmation. Fix: require baseURL to be configured before the coordinator serves an installer that binds a URL, or pin an allowlist of known Darkbloom coordinator hosts, and prompt or warn before overwriting an existing url. Update the threat model for T-040/TB-002 to cover persisted coordinator binding.
findings.title: Installer now persists the serving coordinator URL into provider.toml, so a Host-derived installer URL becomes a lasting provider redirect
